---
title: "Measures overview"
description: "The measures explained in the BNR Public Methods Manual."
---

Different measures answer different questions. A count describes volume; a rate relates events to a population; case fatality describes an outcome among events; and length of stay describes hospital use.

## Measures in this manual

| Measure | Question answered | Usually reported as |
|---|---|---|
| [Number of CVD events](cvd-event-counts.qmd) | How many eligible hospital-registered events were recorded? | Number of events |
| [CVD incidence and event rates](incidence.qmd) | How frequently were eligible events recorded relative to the population? | Events per 100,000 population |
| [CVD case fatality](case-fatality.qmd) | What proportion of eligible hospital events ended in death before discharge? | Percentage |
| [Hospital length of stay](length-of-stay.qmd) | How long did eligible CVD admissions last? | Median days and interquartile range |
| [Mortality](mortality.qmd) | How will deaths and death rates be described? | Number of deaths and population rates |
| [Hypertension](hypertension.qmd) | How will hypertension coverage, care and control be monitored? | Counts, percentages and rates |
| [Diabetes](diabetes.qmd) | How will diabetes coverage, care and outcomes be monitored? | Counts, percentages and rates |

## Choose the right measure

Use counts for workload or burden, rates for population comparisons, case fatality for short-term hospital outcomes, and length of stay or bed-days for hospital use. No single measure gives a complete account of population health or service performance.

::: {.callout-warning title="Similar labels can hide different definitions"}
Two statistics called “incidence” or “mortality” may use different sources, denominators or age-adjustment methods. Use the definition accompanying the BNR output before making a comparison.
:::
